samples.summary: PPTX `hasColor` guard only rejects the bare `''` string, not the `{kind:'srgb', value:''}` shape (nor non-hex CSS strings), so the invalid-attribute condition it was added to prevent is still reachable
samples.evidence: `hasColor(c) { return c != null && c !== ''; }` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:180) is a string-identity test on a `StoredColor` union that also has an object arm. The repo's own `resolveStoredColor` doc comment (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:40-43) states the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` shape really occurs. For that shape `hasColor` returns true, `storedColorToThemeColor` (text.ts:186) returns `{kind:'srgb', value:''}`, and `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35-36) emits `<a:srgbClr val=""/>` — exactly the invalid `ST_HexColorRGB` the guard's comment says PowerPoint rejects. Same gap for HTML-paste values: docs `view/clipboard.ts:150-154` copies browser CSS verbatim, so `color: 'rgb(255, 0, 0)'` reaches the same sink and is emitted as `val="RGB(255,0,0)"`. The docs side of this PR added `toDocxHexColor` validation for precisely this input class; the slides sink was left with only escaping, so no attribute injection is possible (escapeXmlAttr at color.ts:35), which is why this is robustness rather than a vulnerability.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/model/color.ts for the StoredColor union and '' semantics
grep style.backgroundColor across packages to find the HTML-paste producer

samples.summary: `<w:color>`/`<w:shd w:fill>` no longer pass through `escapeXmlAttr`; safety now rests entirely on `toDocxHexColor`'s return-shape invariant with nothing enforcing it
samples.evidence: Before this delta the sinks were `escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#',''))`; now they interpolate `toDocxHexColor(...)`'s result raw (docx-style-map.ts:123,127 and docx-exporter.ts:321). I traced every return path of `toDocxHexColor` (lines 56-74) and all of them yield only `[0-9A-F]{6}` — the 6/3/8-hex arms return validated substrings, and the rgb() arm returns `Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(Number(x))))` rendered via `toString(16).padStart(2,'0')`, with NaN filtered at line 71 — so no injection is possible today, and `$` in JS is end-of-input (no trailing-newline escape). The residual risk is purely future-proofing: any later arm added to this function (e.g. a CSS named-color or `hsl()` map that echoes input) would silently become an attribute-injection sink because the escaping backstop was removed. Cheap hardening: keep `escapeXmlAttr` around the interpolation, or assert the `/^[0-9A-F]{6}$/` shape on return.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:53-128 and traced each return path
grep w:fill=|w:color w:val= across packages/docs/src for other unescaped sinks
read packages/docs/src/export/docx-templates.ts and docx-exporter.ts for remaining raw interpolations

samples.summary: Dropping unrecognized color forms can make text that was visually hidden in the editor render in the default ink in the exported DOCX
samples.evidence: `toDocxHexColor` returns undefined for any form outside hex/`rgb()`/`rgba()` — e.g. `hsl(0,0%,100%)`, `color(display-p3 …)`, or a CSS named color such as `white` (docx-style-map.ts:74). Run color then falls through to the document default (docx-style-map.ts:122) instead of the near-invisible color the author chose, so white-on-white "hidden" text becomes plainly legible in the exported file. Low impact: the characters are present in `word/document.xml` either way, so this only changes visual, not actual, confidentiality — and DOCX import stores `#`+hex, so the vector needs an HTML paste of an `hsl()`/named color. Raising it only because export fidelity around color is exactly what this delta changes.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:147-155 (which CSS forms enter the model)

finding.summary: DOCX table-cell `w:shd w:fill` is still interpolated unescaped — the sibling of the injection this delta just fixed for run properties
finding.evidence: This delta hardens `buildRunPropertiesXml` so `color`/`backgroundColor` go through `escapeXmlAttr` before landing in `<w:color w:val="…">` / `<w:shd w:fill="…">` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:79,83). The identical sink one level up is left raw: `DocxExporter.tableToXml` does `const hex = cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#','')` and emits `<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${hex}"/>` with no escaping (docx-exporter.ts:310-311). `CellStyle.backgroundColor` is a plain `string` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:441) and is populated verbatim from untrusted import: the DOCX importer sets `result.backgroundColor = '#' + fill` straight from the `w:shd/@w:fill` attribute value (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:171-174), which the XML parser has already entity-decoded. Attack chain: attacker crafts a .docx whose table cell carries `w:fill="a"/><w:p>…"`, a victim imports it (value becomes `#a"/><w:p>…`) and re-exports/shares as .docx; the exporter writes that string into the attribute, closing `w:fill="` and injecting arbitrary attacker-chosen OOXML into `word/document.xml` (and into header1.xml/footer1.xml, which route through the same `blockToXml`→`tableToXml`). Because it is arbitrary element injection into a Word document opened by a third party, it can escalate beyond corruption (e.g. injected field/`w:instrText` constructs), and it also defeats escaping-based expectations set by the diff. `escapeXmlAttr` in docx-style-map.ts:25 is module-private, so the exporter cannot currently reuse it — export it (or route cell fills through a shared helper) and escape at line 311.

verdict.reason: The described sink does not exist in this tree. docx-exporter.ts:319 computes the cell fill as `toDocxHexColor(cell.style.backgroundColor)` and only emits `<w:shd … w:fill="${cellFill}"/>` at line 321 when that normalizer returns a value; there is no `backgroundColor.replace('#','')` raw interpolation anywhere in the file. `toDocxHexColor` (docx-style-map.ts:53-75) returns only `undefined` or a string built from strictly regex-validated hex (`/^[0-9a-fA-F]{3}|{6}|{8}$/`, uppercased) or from clamped numeric RGB channels rendered via `toString(16).padStart(2,'0')`, so an imported value such as `#a"/><w:p>` matches no branch and falls through to `return undefined` (line 74), dropping the attribute instead of injecting. The finding's supporting premises are also wrong: the helper is exported (docx-style-map.ts:53) and imported by the exporter (docx-exporter.ts:4-8), and the run-level sink at docx-style-map.ts:121-128 uses the same normalizer rather than `escapeXmlAttr`, so no raw/escaped asymmetry exists. A repo-wide grep for `w:fill`/`w:shd` in packages/docs/src shows only these two emission sites, both normalized, so the header1.xml/footer1.xml path through blockToXml→tableToXml hits the same guarded line 321.
